# Public-source code in libGLcore

Much of `libGLcore.so` is not board code. The software renderer, the display-list machinery, the pixel paths and the name tables descend from the OpenGL sample implementation that SGI published, which this repository carries as the `ogl-sample` submodule. This chapter gives each such routine of the 6.5.30m N32 library its own entry: what it does, the public source file that holds the same routine, and whether it reaches the board. The board-specific routines are in [libglcore.md](libglcore.md), [functions.md](functions.md) and [opengl.md](opengl.md); the routines of the CRIME-specific directories are left to those chapters.

Public source: the sample implementation under `ogl-sample/gfx/lib/opengl`. Paths in the entries are relative to `ogl-sample`. The shipped source file of a routine is the heading it sits under, for example `so_accumop.c`; the sample file that holds the same routine is named in the entry.

Labels follow [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md). An entry is **Established** only where the whole routine was read against the public body. **Inferred** entries are matched to the public routine by its name, its direct calls and the extent of its source, and were not read end to end. Each routine has an entry for the N32 library of the IP32CRM32 build (`usr/gfx/arch/IP32CRM32/libGLcore.so`). Where the o32 build (`usr/gfx/arch/IP32CRM/libGLcore.so`) of the same routine makes the same number of calls and has a similar size, it has its own entry at its own address, inferred unless its body was read in full against the public source, as for the o32 entries marked Established; those entries leave out routines whose description depends on structure offsets or sizes, which differ between the builds. The two builds never share code, so no entry counts for both.

Routines whose name differs from the public one only by a vendor suffix (`EXT`, `SGI`, `SGIS`) or an assembly marker (`Mips`, `_asm`) are matched to the public routine of the unmarked name and say so in the entry. Several of the Mips-marked routines are the assembly replacements that the public source switches in for its own C versions.

The list-compile and list-replay entry points of `g_lcomp.s` and `g_lexec.s` come from the generator specification `ogl-sample/gfx/lib/opengl/generated/listcomp.ls`, which the public sample carries without the generated source. Each of their entries cites the specification, checks the record size against the layout rule it gives where the call's arguments are plain values, and for a replay routine names the public entry point that jumps through the same dispatch-table slot. They are all inferred.

Direct calls that the disassembly labels with the name of a neighbouring symbol are calls to file-local routines.

## Software renderer (soft)

### so_accumop.c

- `Load` in usr/gfx/arch/IP32CRM32/libGLcore.so: loads the accumulation buffer from the colour buffer, multiplying each component by a value and storing it in the accumulator's fixed-point cells, and it occupies 1084 bytes at address 0xd9bb2f0; the public sample-implementation source gfx/lib/opengl/glcore/s_accum.c holds the same routine, matched by name, the shipped routine making one call through procedure pointers, and its body holds no constant address of a board register window and calls no CRIME-specific routine. Inferred.
- `Accumulate` in usr/gfx/arch/IP32CRM32/libGLcore.so: adds the colour buffer's pixels times a value to the accumulation buffer's cells over the clip rectangle, and it occupies 1304 bytes at address 0xd9bb730; the public sample-implementation source gfx/lib/opengl/glcore/s_accum.c holds the same routine, matched by name, the shipped routine making one call through procedure pointers, and its body holds no constant address of a board register window and calls no CRIME-specific routine. Inferred.
- `Mult` in usr/gfx/arch/IP32CRM32/libGLcore.so: multiplies every cell of the accumulation buffer in the clip rectangle by a value, and it occupies 1092 bytes at address 0xd9bbc50; the public sample-implementation source gfx/lib/opengl/glcore/s_accum.c holds the same routine, matched by name, neither the shipped routine nor the public body calling anything, and its body holds no constant address of a board register window and calls no CRIME-specific routine.
